execution.method_note: No Python PostgreSQL driver could be installed in this environment - the configuration requires postgresql+psycopg and neither the package index nor the distribution archive is reachable - so the migrations were rendered with `alembic upgrade head --sql` and executed by psql against the real server. The DDL is Alembic's own and every statement ran; what this does not exercise is the application connecting through SQLAlchemy, which stays unverified and is reported as such.

orm_metadata_drift.finding: `migrations/env.py` declares target_metadata from three modules, which between them map 44 tables. The database the same migrations build has 64 tables plus alembic_version. The 20 undeclared ones are WP-05 through WP-08 - source policy, raw snapshots, canonicalization and the evidence store - which were written as hand-authored migrations with no ORM module anywhere in pgx/infrastructure/db/. The 22 undeclared columns were added to three mapped tables by later migrations without updating the model. `alembic revision --autogenerate` run against this database would therefore propose dropping 20 tables and 22 columns. env.py's own comment names this hazard and says WP-22's and WP-23's tables were added to the list for exactly this reason; WP-05 through WP-08 were not.
orm_metadata_drift.resolution: Reported, not repaired. Writing 20 table definitions is new architecture and is outside Execution Wave 1. Until it is done, autogenerate must not be trusted against this schema.
